name: Snapping Hip Syndrome - External
definition: Audible or palpable lateral snapping caused most commonly by iliotibial band or gluteus maximus moving over the greater trochanter.

investigations.principle: Usually clinical; dynamic ultrasound can demonstrate snapping.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Surgery is rarely required and reserved for persistent disabling cases.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Shroni/Snayu mechanical phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Audible or palpable lateral snapping caused most commonly by iliotibial band or gluteus maximus moving over the greater trochanter.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
